points.title: 早年成长
points.description: 1564年4月23日（受洗日），莎士比亚出生于英格兰沃里克郡的斯特拉福德镇，是约翰·莎士比亚和玛丽·阿登的第三个孩子。他的父亲是一位成功的 glove-maker 和当地官员，母亲则来自富裕的农业家庭。莎士比亚在当地的文法学校接受教育，学习拉丁语、古典文学和修辞学，这些知识后来深刻影响他的戏剧创作。1582年，18岁的莎士比亚与26岁的安妮·海瑟薇结婚，婚后育有三个孩子：苏珊娜和双胞胎哈姆奈特与朱迪思。
points.descriptionEn: William Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon, Warwickshire, England, on April 23, 1564 (baptized), as the third child of John Shakespeare, a successful glove-maker and local official, and Mary Arden, from a prosperous farming family. He received education at the local grammar school, studying Latin, classical literature, and rhetoric, which profoundly influenced his later dramatic works. In 1582, at the age of 18, Shakespeare married Anne Hathaway, who was 26, and they had three children: Susanna and twins Hamnet and Judith.

points.title: 戏剧生涯开端
points.description: 1585年至1592年间，莎士比亚离开斯特拉福德前往伦敦，开始了他的戏剧生涯。这一时期被称为他的'失落岁月'，历史记录较少。据推测，他最初在剧院做马夫、演员，后来逐渐成为编剧和股东。1592年，伦敦剧作家罗伯特·格林在临终前写文章攻击莎士比亚为'傲慢的乌鸦'，这表明莎士比亚已经崭露头角，开始引起同行注意。这一时期，莎士比亚可能已经开始创作他的早期历史剧和喜剧，如《亨利六世》三部曲和《错误的喜剧》。
points.descriptionEn: Between 1585 and 1592, Shakespeare left Stratford for London, beginning his theatrical career. This period, known as his 'lost years,' has limited historical records. It is believed that he initially worked as a horse handler and actor in theaters, gradually becoming a playwright and shareholder. In 1592, London playwright Robert Greene attacked Shakespeare as an 'upstart crow' in his deathbed writing, indicating Shakespeare was already making his mark and gaining attention from peers. During this time, Shakespeare may have begun writing his early histories and comedies, such as the Henry VI trilogy and The Comedy of Errors.

points.title: 创作巅峰期
points.description: 1594年，莎士比亚成为宫内大臣剧团（后改名为国王剧团）的成员和股东，这是他职业生涯的转折点。在接下来的十年里，他创作了大量经典作品，包括《罗密欧与朱丽叶》、《仲夏夜之梦》、《威尼斯商人》、《理查三世》、《亨利四世》等。这一时期，莎士比亚的戏剧在伦敦的环球剧院等场所上演，深受观众欢迎。他不仅创作剧本，还参与演出，并在商业上取得成功。莎士比亚在这一时期积累了财富，于1597年购买了斯特拉福德第二大房产'新宫'，显示了他经济上的成功。
points.descriptionEn: In 1594, Shakespeare became a member and shareholder of the Lord Chamberlain's Men (later renamed the King's Men), marking a turning point in his career. Over the next decade, he wrote numerous classic works including Romeo and Juliet, A Midsummer Night's Dream, The Merchant of Venice, Richard III, and Henry IV. During this period, Shakespeare's plays were performed at venues like the Globe Theatre in London, gaining great popularity with audiences. He not only wrote plays but also acted and achieved commercial success. Shakespeare accumulated wealth during this time, purchasing New Place in Stratford in 1597, his second-largest property, demonstrating his financial success.

points.title: 悲剧与传奇创作
points.description: 1603年詹姆斯一世继位后，莎士比亚的剧团被命名为国王剧团，获得皇家赞助。这一时期，莎士比亚创作了他最著名的悲剧作品，包括《哈姆雷特》、《奥赛罗》、《李尔王》、《麦克白》和《安东尼与克莉奥佩特拉》。这些作品探索了人性的黑暗面、权力、嫉妒和道德困境。1610年左右，莎士比亚开始创作传奇剧，如《暴风雨》、《冬天的故事》和《辛白林》，这些作品融合了悲剧与喜剧元素，带有和解与宽恕的主题。1613年，莎士比亚可能从伦敦戏剧界退休，返回斯特拉福德。
points.descriptionEn: After James I ascended the throne in 1603, Shakespeare's company was renamed the King's Men and received royal patronage. During this period, Shakespeare wrote his most famous tragedies including Hamlet, Othello, King Lear, Macbeth, and Antony and Cleopatra. These works explored the darker aspects of human nature, power, jealousy, and moral dilemmas. Around 1610, Shakespeare began writing romances such as The Tempest, The Winter's Tale, and Cymbeline, which blended tragic and comic elements with themes of reconciliation and forgiveness. In 1613, Shakespeare likely retired from the London theater scene and returned to Stratford.

points.title: 晚年生活
points.description: 1613年莎士比亚返回斯特拉福德后度过了晚年生活。他继续与伦敦的剧团保持联系，但创作活动明显减少。1616年4月23日（与他的生日同一天），莎士比亚在斯特拉福德去世，享年52岁。他被安葬在 Holy Trinity Church，墓碑上刻有他著名的墓志铭。莎士比亚去世后，他的好友约翰·海明斯和亨利·康德尔于1623年出版了第一部莎士比亚戏剧集，被称为'第一对开本'，收录了36部戏剧，为后世保存了莎士比亚的大部分作品。莎士比亚的遗嘱中，他将大部分财产留给了大女儿苏珊娜，只给妻子'我的第二张最好的床'，这一细节成为后世讨论的焦点。
points.descriptionEn: After returning to Stratford in 1613, Shakespeare spent his remaining years there. He maintained connections with the London theater companies but his creative activities significantly decreased. On April 23, 1616 (coinciding with his birthday), Shakespeare died in Stratford at the age of 52. He was buried in Holy Trinity Church, with his famous epitaph on the gravestone. After his death, his friends John Heminges and Henry Condell published the First Folio in 1623, containing 36 plays and preserving most of Shakespeare's works for posterity. In his will, Shakespeare left most of his property to his eldest daughter Susanna, leaving his wife 'my second best bed,' a detail that has been the subject of much discussion.

supporter.zh: 莎士比亚被广泛认为是英语文学史上最伟大的作家，他的作品深刻影响了世界文学和戏剧发展。他的戏剧不仅展现了卓越的语言艺术和人物塑造能力，还探索了永恒的人性主题。莎士比亚创造了数百个生动角色，从国王到平民，从英雄到恶棍，每个角色都具有复杂的人性。他的作品被翻译成几乎所有主要语言，在全球舞台上持续演出，证明了其跨越时空的艺术价值。莎士比亚的语言创新、丰富的比喻和深刻的洞察力使他成为英语文学的基石，他的成语和表达方式已融入日常语言。
supporter.en: Shakespeare is widely regarded as the greatest writer in the English language, with works that profoundly influenced world literature and drama. His plays demonstrate exceptional linguistic artistry and character development while exploring timeless human themes. Shakespeare created hundreds of vivid characters, from kings to commoners, from heroes to villains, each possessing complex humanity. His works have been translated into nearly every major language and continue to be performed worldwide, demonstrating their timeless artistic value. Shakespeare's linguistic innovations, rich metaphors, and profound insights have made him a cornerstone of English literature, with his phrases and expressions integrated into everyday language.

critic.zh: 批评者指出莎士比亚作品存在一些历史局限性，包括对女性的刻板描绘和种族主义倾向。他的女性角色往往局限于传统的女性气质，如奥菲利娅的被动和麦克白夫人的野心导致的毁灭。此外，《威尼斯商人》中的夏洛克等角色被批评为强化了反犹太主义刻板印象。莎士比亚的历史剧也常被批评为简化复杂历史事件，为政治目的服务。一些现代学者还质疑莎士比亚作品的原创性，认为他借鉴了前人的故事和情节，只是以卓越的文学技巧进行了改编。他的'第二张最好的床'遗嘱也引发了关于他对妻子态度的争议。
critic.en: Critics point out certain historical limitations in Shakespeare's work, including stereotypical portrayals of women and racist tendencies. His female characters often conform to traditional femininity, such as Ophelia's passivity and Lady Macbeth's ambition leading to destruction. Additionally, characters like Shylock in The Merchant of Venice have been criticized for reinforcing anti-Semitic stereotypes. Shakespeare's histories are also often criticized for simplifying complex historical events and serving political purposes. Some modern scholars question the originality of Shakespeare's work, suggesting he borrowed stories and plots from predecessors, merely adapting them with exceptional literary skill. His bequest of 'my second best bed' in his will has also sparked controversy about his attitude toward his wife.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，莎士比亚已成为一个文化符号，代表着英语文学的巅峰。他的作品不仅是文学经典，也是全球文化的重要组成部分，被改编成电影、歌剧、芭蕾舞等多种艺术形式。莎士比亚研究（莎士比亚学）已成为一个专门的学术领域。在流行文化中，莎士比亚的名字常被用来代表文学成就的最高标准，'莎士比亚式的'已成为描述复杂人物和情节的形容词。尽管存在争议，莎士比亚的作品持续影响着现代文学、电影和戏剧，他的主题和人物原型仍在当代创作中被重新诠释。莎士比亚的全球影响力使他成为英国文化最重要的输出之一，也是世界文学遗产的核心组成部分。
objective.en: In academic circles and popular culture, Shakespeare has become a cultural symbol representing the pinnacle of English literature. His works are not only literary classics but also an essential part of global culture, adapted into films, operas, ballets, and other art forms. Shakespeare studies (Shakespearean scholarship) has developed into a specialized academic field. In popular culture, Shakespeare's name is often used to represent the highest standard of literary achievement, and 'Shakespearean' has become an adjective describing complex characters and plots. Despite controversies, Shakespeare's works continue to influence modern literature, film, and theater, with his themes and character prototypes being reinterpreted in contemporary creations. Shakespeare's global influence makes him one of the most important cultural exports of England and a core component of world literary heritage.

self.zh: 生存还是毁灭，这是一个值得考虑的问题。
self.en: To be, or not to be: that is the question.

others.zh: 他不属于一个时代，而属于所有时代。
others.en: He was not of an age, but for all time.
